title: The Savoy Male and Female College
text:
After living for a time in Bonham, they moved to Oklahoma. They now live in Oklahoma City, where Mrs. Smith continues to teach music and the art of dancing. They have one son, Dee Smith, and three daughters, Lela Mae, Elizabeth, and Janetta Lou.

Miss Lily Lacy, one of the later art teachers, began her work at the College when she was only eighteen years old and just out of Carlton College in Bonham. Since then she has continued the study of art widely, and has taught in Grayson College at Whitewright, Carlton College in Bonham, Carr-Burdette College in Sherman, and Kendall College, Enid, Oklahoma. She lives in Bonham and is teaching a private class.


COMMERCIAL TEACHERS

Except in the single case of Mr. Leon C. Reynolds, scant information is available on the men who established the commercial department of the Savoy College in the seventies and carried the work forward effectively. Mr. George Hardsaw, Mr. J. E. of Finger, Mr. James L. George, Mr. J. D. Warren, and Mr. W. P. Marcy, all left the impress of their capable teaching on a generation of Savoy graduates and their business training successfully, but Mr. Reynolds is the only one with whom contact has been established or concerning whom much information is available. He still lives and at the age of seventy-four years is actively engaged in the printing business in Dallas. Because his connection with the Savoy College is thus continuing and is broadly represented in the printing and publishing traditions that bind him in so intimately with the College history, his life sketch, written by him out himself, is given as a fitting conclusion to this biographical chapter.
